title: no_route SLA leg aborts on runtime errors — three checks never run, suite false-greens
evidence:
sim._spawn_packet(1, 20, "email") # 20 lives in another wedge, unconnected
	check(str(sim.drops[0].reason) == "no_route" and int(sim.drops[0].pipe) == -1,
		"no_route: unroutable packet drops with an attributable no_route record")
	check(int(sim.sla["email"].dropped) == 1, "no_route drop counts against the class")
	check(not bool(sim.sla["email"].loss_breach), "isolation: a single no_route does not latch the loss SLA")
--- observed run: "SCRIPT ERROR: Out of bounds get index '0' (on base: 'Array') at: _no_route_and_unreachable_isolation (res://tests/test_sim_sla.gd:115)" — then "SUITE RESULT: PASS (0 failure(s))" with NO 'ok' lines printed for these three checks.
detail: A1 requires 'every E2 test contract demonstrable'; the attributable-no_route pin errors mid-function, its checks never execute, and the gate still reports PASS. Not 'proven by a mutation leg' as the spec AC claims.
recommended_fix: Fix the underlying _pick_next_pipe nil crash (see sibling finding), then rerun; the un-vacuated 'single no_route does not latch' check will fail red until the latch logic also gains a sample floor.

title: SimCore no_route path crashes on empty routes and single no_route drop latches loss SLA
detail: Spec I/O matrix promises 'a packet with no route drops WITH a no_route record' / 'Manual spawn to an unreachable destination: recorded, attributable'. Actual: typed-nil script error, packet stranded invisible to SLA; and one no_route drop latches the 30% loss breach (100% of 1 sample).
recommended_fix: Use untyped 'var r = routes.get(dst)' before the null check; in _record_drop, exclude no_route drops from the loss latch (or require a minimum denominator) so single unreachable spawns cannot latch a breach.

title: run_tests.gd abort guard misses nested-function aborts — false green persists
detail: The guard only fires when run_all itself returns null. The observed isolation-test abort happened inside a nested sync function: run_all still returned int, three checks vanished, and the suite stayed green — exactly the false-green the comment claims to prevent.
recommended_fix: Also fail when script errors occur during a script's run: track Godot error-hook counts or have test_base register errors per active script and count them as failures.

title: Determinism capture applies commands at tick 300, replay test at tick 120 — 'can never drift' overstated
evidence:
tool: "		if t == ticks / 3:
			for c in cmds:"  vs test: "		if t == 120:
			for c in REPLAY_CMDS:"  — shared claim: "## The replay-evidence command stream — ONE definition shared by
## tests/test_sim_replay.gd and tools/determinism_log.gd so the committed
## capture and its sibling test can never drift apart."
detail: REPLAY_CMDS/REPLAY_TICKS are shared, but command application timing differs (300 vs 120) and 'timing is state' per the test's own pin — so the committed capture is not the replay test's scenario. Both still prove identity independently (capture regenerates byte-identical).
recommended_fix: Move the application tick (e.g. 120) into test_sim_base next to REPLAY_CMDS/REPLAY_TICKS and use it in both files.
